question: How much of the field flow-matching error is irreducible observation noise, and how much normal-data structure has each network learned beyond an analytic Gaussian predictor?
timing: Specified after the R8 normal audit and architecture selection, while the frozen likelihood study runs. Does not change that study or use its anomaly results.
inputs: The exact 1024 normal validation maps, shape-noise draws, interpolation noise and times from audit_normal.py. No public test or synthetic anomalies.
baselines: Unit-variance independent Gaussian velocity using the existing global training normalization.
Independent Gaussian velocity with mean and variance fitted on all 16160 clean training maps separately for each mask-coverage count, plus the known shape-noise variance.

Privileged oracle velocity given each clean validation image and the known observation-noise variance. This uses information unavailable at deployment and is only a diagnostic lower bound on expected squared error.
comparison: Use the same realized velocity targets for all references and all six saved normal model audits. Report per-time and uniform-time paired errors, reference-to-oracle gap and fraction of that gap explained by each network; do not interpret the latter as anomaly-detection performance.
numerical_checks: Check Gaussian conditional mean and variance algebra by simulation and a direct conditional-Gaussian covariance calculation before evaluating real normal maps.
resources: CPU-only on the already authorized erdos-3242 head, with a 2-CPU quota and bounded memory; no TPU ownership changes, bucket access or production mutation.
